newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD opposed to Maastricht II without jobs charter.
newsitem.headline: SPD opposed to Maastricht II without jobs charter.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) will not approve a second Maastricht treaty on European monetary union (EMU) if it does not include a social charter, deputy SPD leader Heidemarie Wieczorek-Zeul said on Thursday.
Wieczorek-Zeul told the German lower house of parliament in a debate about EMU the German government was the only government in Europe that wanted currency union without an active jobs market policy.
The SPD deputy leader said that her party was in favour of currency union. She said the introduction of the euro was urgently needed and that it made sense economically and politically.
But she warned that the euro should not be used as an excuse to cut social benefits and erode away the rights of employees.
Wieczorek-Zeul said the criteria to qualify for EMU should be interpreted according to the Maastricht treaty.
